title: Working Out the Benefit Payable on a Submitted Rider Line
content:
Basis on which the claims desk works out what one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders pays on a line a provider has submitted.

## 1. The amount the benefit is taken from

The benefit a rider pays on a submitted line is worked out from the allowed amount the line carries and never from what the provider charged. The amount the benefit is taken from is the allowed amount carried by the line standing on the member's benefit history awaiting a decision.

## 2. What is carried into the benefit calculation

The whole of the amount the benefit is taken from is carried into the benefit calculation.

## 3. The deductible

The benefit year's deductible the rider held carries is taken off what is carried into the benefit calculation before any share is applied, on the benefit categories the rider takes its deductible on and only while the rider has paid no line in such a category in the benefit year; preventive care is never subject to a deductible.

## 4. The share

The share taken is the coinsurance percentage the rider held carries for the line's benefit category: the preventive share on preventive dental care, the basic restorative share on basic restorative dental care, the major restorative share on major restorative dental care, the root canal share on endodontic treatment, the gum treatment share on periodontic treatment, the oral surgery share on oral surgery, the denture share on dentures and the implant share on implants, and a benefit category the rider held carries no coinsurance percentage for is not paid at all.

The benefit is that share of what is left after the deductible, rounded to the nearest cent.

## 5. The benefit already paid in the benefit year

Every line counted is one the rider record itself carries, that record covering a single benefit year. The benefit already paid in the benefit year is the figure the rider record shows used toward the benefit year's maximum.

## 6. What is left of the benefit year's maximum

What is left of the benefit year's maximum is the benefit year's maximum the rider held carries less the benefit already paid in the benefit year, and is never less than nothing.

## 7. The figure booked

The figure booked is the lesser of the benefit so worked out and what is left of the benefit year's maximum, rounded to the nearest cent.

## Worked through on hypothetical inputs

Take a submitted line awaiting a decision whose allowed amount is 400.00 USD, for basic restorative dental care, the provider having charged 520.00 USD. Take a rider whose benefit year deductible is 50.00 USD, taken on basic restorative dental care among its categories, no line in any such category having been paid this benefit year; whose basic restorative share is 80 per cent; whose benefit year maximum is 1500.00 USD; and whose record shows 200.00 USD used toward that maximum.

1. The amount the benefit is taken from is the allowed amount the line carries, 400.00 USD. The 520.00 USD the provider charged does not enter the calculation.
2. The whole of that amount is carried into the benefit calculation: 400.00 USD.
3. The deductible of 50.00 USD is taken off first, leaving 350.00 USD.
4. The share for basic restorative dental care is 80 per cent, and 80 per cent of 350.00 USD is 280.00 USD.
5. The benefit already paid in the benefit year is the 200.00 USD the record shows used.
6. What is left of the benefit year's maximum is 1500.00 USD less 200.00 USD, that is 1300.00 USD.
7. The figure booked is the lesser of 280.00 USD and 1300.00 USD, that is **280.00 USD**.

Every figure above is a hypothetical input chosen to show the order the quantities are taken in; none of them is a rate or a term of any rider.
